Not reproducible. `std::process::Child::kill` returns `Ok(())` when the child has already exited (std behavior since Rust 1.72; this crate already needs 1.85+ for `edition2024`), and `wait()` returns the cached status, so retry falls through to `*process = None` and respawns. Checked with the installed toolchain:

```
rustc 1.97.1
try_wait reaped: Some(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(1792)))
kill() after reap -> Ok(())
wait() after reap -> Ok(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(1792)))
```

The Windows std impl has the same guard (treats `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` on an exited handle as `Ok`).

from agentic review: `clamp_window_bounds` panics on a zero-size work area: the `.max(1)` guard guarantees `clamp(min, max)` gets `min > max`, and the call site is in `setup`, so the app fails to launch rather than degrading.

Fixed. Empty or inverted work areas now return an error, so setup logs the fitting failure and still reveals the window instead of panicking. The arithmetic also uses `i64` internally to cover the full Win32 `i32` coordinate domain. Regression tests cover empty and extreme-coordinate work areas.
